quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is a primary cause of single-motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: Turning too wide in a curve is a primary cause of single-motorcycle crashes. This can force your motorcycle off the road or into an object.

questions.question: If you wear a helmet during a crash, you are more likely to:

options.text: Be less likely to survive than someone not wearing a helmet.
Have the same survival chance as someone not wearing a helmet.
Be more likely to survive than someone not wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be more likely to survive than someone not wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the brake pressure. Then slowly re-apply the brake with gentle, steady pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane:

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually provides enough grip for safe riding, except in rain. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: Are helmets required?
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a DOT-approved helmet every time they ride. Helmets are your best protection against head and neck injuries.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle in a curve?

options.text: Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that matches your conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When being passed, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the other driver puts you both in danger.

questions.question: A motorcycle should fit you properly. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely touch the handlebars when you sit on the motorcycle.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when you stand next to the motorcycle.
Your feet should touch the ground comfortably when you sit on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should touch the ground comfortably when you sit on the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground comfortably while you sit on it. Always check the fit before you ride.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Placed on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Loads should be placed over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on their motorcycle.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the best way is to:

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight through your lane when crossing angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your path angle may move you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked because it will help you stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the front brake pressure. Then apply the brake again with slow, controlled pressure.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake stops you the most?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to:
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: When you stop, you should:
questions.explanation: Get into the habit of using both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the driver did not yield to the motorcyclist.
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers do not yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers will yield, even if they should by law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what should you remember?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
Focus on riding your motorcycle and ignore the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of large trucks. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Is eye protection required when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: The law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield offers the best protection.

questions.question: What should you do about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They do not exist if your motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal routine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
One that hides you from other drivers.
One directly next to another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when starting the engine?
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that shows when the engine is on and in neutral.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best foot protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and drive away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and drive away.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches, slow down and downshift. Quickly accelerate away as the dog gets close.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should be part of your normal scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Always looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs longer to stop, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and vehicles may cut in front of you.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as you can.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should generally ride in what formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group of riders stay close together while keeping safe space around each rider. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Shift down to a lower gear immediately.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over bridge gratings, simply relax and steer straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: If you and another vehicle arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right of way?

options.text: Flash your headlight to tell them to go.
You should go through and expect them to stop.

questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: At night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light differences help you see how far away objects are. At night, artificial lighting may distort or hide these helpful shadows and differences.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black letters or symbols. This sign warns drivers about a divided roadway ahead.
